23771618.reason: Only counts divisibility by primes <=floor(sqrt(100001))=316, ignoring larger prime factors. Test 0018 has 27 strengths equal to prime 12553; it returns 8 rather than 27.

23772167.reason: Although its prime list includes 12553, it stops scanning when p>max(strengths)/2, wrongly excluding prime strengths themselves. Test 0018 has maximum strength 12553 and 27 copies of it; it returns 8 rather than 27.

23772314.reason: Searches only divisibility by a strength present in the input, instead of possible common divisors absent from the input. For 5,6,4, divisor 2 supports 6 and 4, but it returns 1 instead of 2.

23772496.reason: Selects only values with the smallest heuristic pairwise-coprime score, then considers only their factors; this does not preserve the optimal divisor. On 9,4,2,3,3,9,8 it selects 8, obtains count 3 for divisor 2, and misses divisor 3 supporting four values.

23772648.reason: Counts raw strengths and newly appended divisor occurrences in the same mutable list. A raw strength that is also an appended divisor is double-counted, and the iteration jumps by that mutated multiplicity. Test 0004 returns 5 rather than the true maximum 4 (divisor 2).
